label: r4c1
name: slim aligned net, 3 epochs
hypothesis: This is r3c3's slim network (compute about 1x the start) with 3 PPO epochs instead of 2. That gives about 168k steps, more than r2c3's 139k. Every 3-epoch run so far kept both seeds learning, while 2-epoch runs collapsed or stalled on one seed. So this should keep r3c3's sample advantage and lift the weak seed. Refuted if the mean is at or below r2c3's 0.47, or if one seed is still under 0.25.
last_analysis: The cheap learned shift-align module beats the costly axial convolutions. Spending compute on samples rather than width helps: the slim r3c3 reached 0.71 on one seed with IoU 0.95. The main risk is the early drift toward DONE. Mean episode length at 25% of training is about 2, and it fully collapsed in r1c3 and r3c2 seed 0 (both 2 epochs or tiny batches). The slim 2-epoch run r3c3 also had one weak seed (0.19). Every 3-epoch run kept both seeds alive (0.55/0.38, 0.47/0.32). Entropy between 0.03 and 0.04 makes no difference within noise. So: (A) the slim net with the more reliable 3 epochs, which still gets about 168k steps; (B) the slim net with 2 epochs and zero-initialised policy and value outputs, so it starts from a uniform policy and does not depend on random output-layer init; (C) both, zero-init plus 3 epochs.
